title: 2012 AMC 12B Problem 10
statement: What is the area of the polygon whose vertices are the points of intersection of the curves \(x^2 + y^2 = 25\) and \((x - 4)^2 + 9y^2 = 81?\)

solutions.text:
From \(x^2+y^2=25\) we get \(y^2=25-x^2.\) Substituting into \((x-4)^2+9y^2=81\) gives \(x^2+x-20=0,\) so \(x=4\) or \(x=-5.\)

The intersection points are \((-5,0),\) \((4,3),\) and \((4,-3).\)

The vertical side from \((4,3)\) to \((4,-3)\) has length \(6,\) and the horizontal distance to \((-5,0)\) is \(9,\) so the area is \(\tfrac12\cdot6\cdot9=27.\)

Thus, the correct answer is B.
hints: Solve the first equation for \(y^2\) and substitute into the second
The three intersection points form a triangle; use one vertical side as the base
